24: def _flaky(fail_times):
25:     """An action that fails its first ``fail_times`` attempts, then succeeds."""
26: 
27:     def action(ctx):
28:         if ctx.attempt <= fail_times:
29:             raise RuntimeError("transient failure #{}".format(ctx.attempt))

34: class PipelineTest(unittest.TestCase):
35:     # -- retry pipelines (needs the config deep-merge AND the retry boundary) --
36: 
37:     def test_retry_succeeds_on_third_attempt(self):
38:         # The task overrides the single-attempt default with a budget of three
39:         # and fails twice before succeeding. This needs the per-task retry
40:         # override to survive the deep-merge *and* the retry boundary to permit
41:         # the third attempt.
42:         report = run_pipeline(
43:             {
44:                 "name": "retry",
45:                 "defaults": {
46:                     "retry": {"max_attempts": 1, "backoff": "constant", "base": 0}
47:                 },
48:                 "tasks": [
49:                     {
50:                         "id": "flaky",
51:                         "action": _flaky(2),
52:                         "retry": {"max_attempts": 3},
53:                     }
54:                 ],
55:             }
56:         )
57:         self.assertEqual(report.state_of("flaky"), State.SUCCEEDED)
58:         self.assertEqual(report.attempts_of("flaky"), 3)
59: 
60:     def test_retry_exhausts_to_permanent_failure(self):
61:         # Five failures against a three-attempt budget: it makes exactly three
62:         # attempts and then fails permanently.
63:         report = run_pipeline(
64:             {
65:                 "name": "retry-exhaust",
66:                 "defaults": {
67:                     "retry": {"max_attempts": 1, "backoff": "constant", "base": 0}
68:                 },
69:                 "tasks": [
70:                     {
71:                         "id": "doomed",
72:                         "action": _flaky(5),
73:                         "retry": {"max_attempts": 3},
74:                     }
75:                 ],
76:             }
77:         )
78:         self.assertEqual(report.state_of("doomed"), State.FAILED)
79:         self.assertEqual(report.attempts_of("doomed"), 3)
80: 
81:     def test_retry_unblocks_downstream(self):
82:         # A flaky task recovers on its second attempt, which must let its
83:         # downstream dependant run to success rather than be skipped.
84:         report = run_pipeline(
85:             {
86:                 "name": "retry-chain",
87:                 "defaults": {
88:                     "retry": {"max_attempts": 1, "backoff": "constant", "base": 0}
89:                 },
90:                 "tasks": [
91:                     {
92:                         "id": "flaky",
93:                         "action": _flaky(1),
94:                         "retry": {"max_attempts": 2},
95:                     },
96:                     {"id": "after", "action": _noop, "deps": ["flaky"]},
97:                 ],
98:             }
99:         )
100:         self.assertEqual(report.state_of("flaky"), State.SUCCEEDED)
101:         self.assertEqual(report.state_of("after"), State.SUCCEEDED)
102:         self.assertEqual(report.attempts_of("flaky"), 2)

104:     # -- priority pipelines (needs the queue tie-break AND the batch guard) ---
105: 
106:     def test_priority_dispatch_order(self):
107:         # Three tasks become ready together; they must dispatch highest-priority
108:         # first even though they are declared low-to-high.
109:         report = run_pipeline(
110:             {
111:                 "name": "prio",
112:                 "concurrency": 5,
113:                 "tasks": [
114:                     {"id": "low", "action": _noop, "priority": 1},
115:                     {"id": "mid", "action": _noop, "priority": 2},

117:                 ],
118:             }

121:         self.assertEqual(report.run_order(), ["high", "mid", "low"])

124:         # Four independent tasks with mixed priorities dispatch in strict
125:         # descending-priority order within the batch.
126:         report = run_pipeline(
127:             {
128:                 "name": "prio4",
129:                 "concurrency": 5,
130:                 "tasks": [
131:                     {"id": "a", "action": _noop, "priority": 1},
132:                     {"id": "b", "action": _noop, "priority": 3},
133:                     {"id": "c", "action": _noop, "priority": 2},
134:                     {"id": "d", "action": _noop, "priority": 5},
135:                 ],
136:             }
137:         )
138:         self.assertTrue(report.ok())
139:         self.assertEqual(report.run_order(), ["d", "b", "c", "a"])
140: 
141:     def test_priority_respected_after_dependency(self):
142:         # Once a root finishes, its two dependants become ready together and
143:         # must run high-priority first.
144:         report = run_pipeline(
145:             {
146:                 "name": "prio-dep",
147:                 "concurrency": 5,
148:                 "tasks": [
149:                     {"id": "root", "action": _noop},
150:                     {"id": "cheap", "action": _noop, "deps": ["root"], "priority": 1},
151:                     {"id": "urgent", "action": _noop, "deps": ["root"], "priority": 8},
152:                 ],
153:             }
154:         )
155:         self.assertTrue(report.ok())
156:         self.assertEqual(report.run_order(), ["root", "urgent", "cheap"])
157: 
158:     # -- resource pipelines (needs the release-by-cost fix) ------------------
159: 
160:     def test_resource_serialized_run_all_finish(self):
161:         # Each task needs the whole pool, so they run strictly one at a time.
162:         # Every task must still finish -- which only happens if each release
163:         # returns the *full* cost so the next task can be admitted.
164:         report = run_pipeline(
165:             {
166:                 "name": "res-serial",

173:                 ],
174:             }

176:         self.assertTrue(report.ok())

184:             {
185:                 "name": "res-peak",

187:                 "concurrency": 5,
188:                 "tasks": [
189:                     {"id": "w1", "action": _noop, "resources": {"mem": 2}},
